input_text: Q: "Context: GL Account 12010020 shows 'Property, plant and 12010020 - Furniture & Fittings-cost' with balance 42,611.00. GL Account 12010910 shows 'Accumulated Depr 12010910 - Accum. Dep Furniture and Fittings' with balance (31,482.00). How should I map these to the master COA?"
output_text:
A: "Map 12010020 to 'Property, Plant & Equipment - Furniture & Fittings (Gross Block)'. Map 12010910 to 'Accumulated Depreciation - Furniture & Fittings'. Net value = 42,611.00 - 31,482.00 = 11,129.00"
Q: "The Malaysian entity shows 'Research Instruments Sdn. Bhd.' with MYR currency. The Indian parent uses INR. How should I handle currency conversion for consolidation?"
A: "Identify the reporting date (e.g., 30 June 2025). Use the MYR/INR exchange rate as of that date from reliable sources (RBI, OANDA). Convert all MYR amounts to INR before consolidation. Maintain both original and converted values in audit trail."
Q: "Entity A uses 'Trade debtors' (Account 14010010) with balance 1,814,549.17. Entity B uses 'Trade Receivables' in balance sheet. Are these the same?"
A: "Yes, both represent 'Accounts Receivable (Trade)' in master COA. 'Trade debtors' and 'Trade Receivables' are synonymous terms. Map both to 'Trade Receivables'."
Q: "GL Account 21010010 shows 'Trade Creditors-Foreign' 579,668.95. Account 21010020 shows 'Trade Creditors-Local' 32,451.31. How to map?"
A: "Both are 'Accounts Payable'. Map to 'Trade Payables' in master COA, but maintain sub-classification: 'Foreign Creditors' and 'Local Creditors' for disclosure purposes."
Q: "File shows 'Right of Use Asset 12060020 - Right of Use Asset-cost' 223,475.00 with accumulated depreciation 12060910 of (146,965.00). How to treat under Ind AS?"
A: "This is an Ind AS 116 lease asset. Map to 'Right-of-Use Assets' (Gross: 223,475.00, Accum Dep: 146,965.00, Net: 76,510.00). Ensure corresponding lease liability is also identified."
Q: "Notes show 'Deferred tax assets (net)' of 28,196 as of June 2025. What components make this up?"
A: "Based on Note 28(c): Includes Expected credit loss (14,000), Unrealised loss on forex (53,843), Business losses (53,843), Property/Equipment differences (65,104), less Unutilised capital allowances (73,213), etc. Total net DTA = 56,110 as of Mar 2025, decreased to 28,196 by June 2025."
Q: "What is 'CPF-Staff' in the Malaysian payroll expenses?"
A: "CPF = Central Provident Fund (Malaysia's employee provident fund). This is equivalent to 'Provident Fund Contributions' in Indian context. Map to 'Employee Benefits Expense - Provident Fund'."
Q: "Account 14025020 shows 'Loan to Chemopharm Sdn Bhd' 1,750,000.00. Note 29 shows Chemopharm is 'Immediate Holding Company'. How to treat?"
A: "This is an intercompany loan to a related party (holding company). In consolidation: 1) Eliminate the loan receivable from subsidiary against loan payable in holding company. 2) Eliminate any interest income/expense. 3) Disclose as related party transaction."
Q: "Account 14050310 shows 'F.Deposit-Maybank' 79,596.39. Where to map?"
A: "This is 'Fixed Deposits with Banks' or 'Bank Deposits > 3 months maturity'. Map to 'Other Financial Assets - Bank Deposits' under Current/Non-current based on maturity."
Q: "The P&L shows 'Sales incentives-Staff' and 'Sales incentives-Provision'. What's the difference?"
A: "'Sales incentives-Staff' is the actual incentive paid/accrued. 'Sales incentives-Provision' is a provision for future incentives. Map both to 'Employee Benefits Expense - Sales Commission/Incentives'. The provision should be reversed when paid."
Q: "Account 14010020 shows 'Other Debtors' with balance (129,280.20) - negative. What does this mean?"
A: "A negative debtor balance typically indicates a credit balance - it's actually a payable. Investigate: Could be advance from customer, overpayment, or misclassification. Flag for review with confidence score 70%."
Q: "Note 20 shows 'Sale of goods' with Domestic and Export categories. How should revenue be segmented?"
A: "Segment revenue as: 1) Domestic Sales, 2) Export Sales. Further classify as 'Manufactured Goods' and 'Traded Goods' if data available. Required for segment reporting under Ind AS 108."
Q: "Account 14022000 shows 'AP Down Payment Payable' 7,878.86. What is this?"
A: "Advance payments to suppliers. Map to 'Advances to Suppliers' or 'Other Payables'. Should be netted against final invoice when goods/services received."
Q: "Multiple bank accounts in different currencies: Alliance Bank - EUR, USD; CIMB Bank - USD; Maybank. How to consolidate?"
A: "1) Convert all foreign currency balances to INR using closing rate. 2) Sum all cash balances. 3) Disclose foreign currency exposure as per Note requirement (Item 6 in checklist)."
Q: "Note 21 shows 'Interest income from banks' and 'Interest income from others'. How to map?"
A: "Both are 'Other Income - Interest Received'. Maintain sub-classification: 'From Banks' and 'From Others' for better analysis."
Q: "Human Resource Expenses show 'Sosco-Directors' and 'Sosco-Staff'. What is Sosco?"
A: "SOCSO = Social Security Organization (Malaysian social security). Equivalent to ESIC in India. Map to 'Employee Benefits Expense - Social Security Contributions'."
Q: "Account 12025911 shows 'Accumulated Depr machinery' (43,017.33). Account 12025330 shows 'Machinery-cost' 397,202.33. What's the net block?"
A: "Net Block = 397,202.33 - 43,017.33 = 354,185.00. Depreciation rate = 43,017.33/397,202.33 = ~10.8% indicating ~1-2 years of depreciation if straight-line."
Q: "Note 24 shows 'Employee benefits expense' with Salaries (44.83), Contributions to funds (-0.01), Staff welfare (-). Why negative?"
A: "Negative amounts in expense could be reversals of excess provisions, refunds, or accounting errors. Flag for manual review with confidence score 65%. Could be data entry issue."
Q: "Account 14006000 shows 'Inventory - Goods in transit' 16,441.03. How to value?"
A: "Goods in transit should be included in inventory if risk/reward transferred. Value at cost. Ensure it's included in total inventory for ratio analysis."
Q: "Note 33 shows depreciation rates. How to verify if correct?"
A: "Calculate implied rates: For Computers (Gross: 74,751, Dep: 60,123 = 80% depreciated - likely 4-5 year life). For Machinery (Gross: 416,878, Dep: 200,930 = 48% - likely 5-10 year life). Flag if rates differ significantly from tax/accounting policies.
Q: "File has 'Gratuity and other post-employment benefit plans' under Note 38. How to map?"
A: "This is 'Employee Benefits Expense - Gratuity'. In balance sheet, it appears as 'Provision for gratuity - current' and 'non-current'. Ensure actuarial valuation included."
Q: "Account shows 'Unrealised loss on foreign exchange' in deferred tax note. Is this P&L or balance sheet?"
A: "Unrealised forex loss on monetary items is P&L item (Finance cost/income). The tax effect is deferred tax asset/liability. Map forex loss to 'Finance Costs - Forex Loss'."
Q: "Note 27 shows 'Sales return' with provision. How to account?"
A: "Sales returns should reduce revenue. Provision for sales returns is a liability. Map to 'Revenue - Less: Sales Returns' and 'Provision for Sales Returns' respectively."
Q: "Multiple accounts for similar items: 'Tools & Equipment-cost', 'Office Equipment-cost', 'Computers-cost'. Should these be combined?"
A: "For reporting, combine as 'Property, Plant & Equipment - Office Equipment' (include Computers, Furniture, Tools). For fixed asset register, maintain separately."
Q: "The ratio analysis shows Debt Service Coverage Ratio of 199.75. What components are needed?"
A: "DSCR = (Net Profit + Depreciation + Interest + Other non-cash items) / (Interest + Principal repayment). From data: Numerator = 2,978,504.92, Denominator = 14,910.87."
Q: "Note 34 shows 'Impairment allowance for doubtful advances' and 'Allowance for expected credit loss'. Difference?"
A: "Both are 'Impairment/Provision for Bad Debts'. 'Doubtful advances' is for loans/advances. 'ECL on trade receivables' is for customers. Map both to 'Allowance for Doubtful Debts'."
Q: "Account 21011510 shows 'Cred Alloc-Import duty' 23,930.02. Where does this go?"
A: "Import duty on purchases. Should be capitalized to inventory cost. Map to 'Inventory - Add: Import Duty' or 'Customs Duty'."
Q: "There's 'Contract liabilities' in balance sheet but no amount. What is this?"
A: "Contract liabilities = advance from customers under Ind AS 115. If balance is zero, entity may not have advance receipts. Map to 'Advance from Customers' when present."
Q: "Note 47 shows 'Expenditure on Corporate Social Responsibility'. Where to map?"
A: "CSR expense under Indian Companies Act. Map to 'Other Expenses - Corporate Social Responsibility'."
Q: "The file shows 'Deferred tax: Recognised/(reversed) in other comprehensive income'. How to handle?"
A: "Tax effects of items in OCI (like forex on foreign operations, actuarial gains). Map to 'Other Comprehensive Income' with tax effect shown separately.
Q: "Entity has 'Right of use assets' and separate 'Lease liabilities'. How to ensure they balance?"
A: "ROU Asset = Present value of lease payments. Lease Liability = Same initially. Check: ROU Asset 223,475, Accum Dep 146,965 = Net 76,510. Lease liability should be similar (split current/non-current)."
Q: "Note shows 'Government grant income'. Is this revenue or capital?"
A: "Government grants related to assets = Deduct from asset cost (Ind AS 20). Grants related to income = Recognize in P&L over period. Map to 'Other Income - Government Grants'."
Q: "Account 14015000 shows 'Prepayments' 38,304.62. What typically includes?"
A: "Prepaid insurance, rent, subscriptions, taxes. Map to 'Prepaid Expenses' under Current Assets."
Q: "File shows 'Trade Receivable ageing' requirement in checklist. How to generate?"
A: "Age receivables as: Current, 1-30 days, 31-60, 61-90, 90+. Use invoice dates. Required for Ind AS disclosure."
Q: "Note 29 shows related party transactions. What disclosures needed?"
A: "Disclose: Nature of relationship, transactions during period, balances at period end, terms, provisions for doubtful debts. Required under Ind AS 24.
Q: "Subsidiary has loan to parent company (Chemopharm) of 1,750,000. Parent shows loan from subsidiary of 1,750,000. How to eliminate?"
A: "In consolidation: Dr. Loan Payable (Parent) 1,750,000, Cr. Loan Receivable (Subsidiary) 1,750,000. Also eliminate any interest income/expense between them."
Q: "Parent sells goods to subsidiary worth 500,000 at 20% margin. Subsidiary has 40% inventory unsold at year-end. How much unrealized profit to eliminate?"
A: "Unrealized profit = 500,000 × 20% margin × 40% unsold = 40,000. Elimination: Dr. Group Revenue 500,000, Cr. Group COGS 460,000, Cr. Inventory 40,000."
Q: "Subsidiary is 80% owned. Minority interest in subsidiary's net assets is 2,000,000. How to present?"
A: "Show 'Minority Interest' of 2,000,000 in Equity section of consolidated balance sheet. In P&L, deduct minority share of subsidiary's profit."
Q: "Parent and subsidiary have intercompany sales of 1,000,000 each. Both show as revenue. How to consolidate?"
A: "Eliminate entirely: Dr. Group Revenue 1,000,000, Cr. Group COGS 1,000,000 (assuming no unsold inventory). Net effect zero."
Q: "Subsidiary pays dividend of 200,000 to parent. How to eliminate?"
A: "Parent's dividend income (200,000) eliminated against subsidiary's dividend paid. In consolidated cash flow, it's intra-group (non-cash)."
Q: "Parent guarantees subsidiary's bank loan. Subsidiary shows loan, parent shows contingent liability. How to consolidate?"
A: "No elimination in balance sheet (it's a guarantee). Disclose as contingent liability and related party transaction."
Q: "Subsidiary has different year-end (Mar 31) vs parent (Dec 31). How to consolidate?"
A: "Use subsidiary's financials for period ending Dec 31 (require interim accounts). Alternative: Use subsidiary's Mar 31 accounts with adjustments for significant transactions in Jan-Mar."
Q: "Subsidiary is foreign (Malaysia) with functional currency MYR. Parent is India with INR. How to translate?"
A: "1) Assets/Liabilities: Closing rate. 2) Equity: Historical rates. 3) P&L: Average rate. 4) Exchange differences go to Other Comprehensive Income (OCI)."
Q: "Joint venture (50% owned) using equity method. JV's net assets = 10,000,000, profit = 1,000,000. How to consolidate?"
A: "Equity method: Show investment at cost + share of post-acquisition profits. Balance sheet: Investment in JV = 5,000,000 + 500,000 = 5,500,000. P&L: Share of profit = 500,000."
Q: "After all eliminations, consolidated trial balance doesn't balance by 50,000. Common causes?"
A: "1) Unequal intercompany amounts. 2) Forex differences not eliminated. 3) Unrealized profit calculated incorrectly. 4) Minority interest error. Check intercompany reconciliations."
Q: "Subsidiary declares bonus to employees. Parent accrues provision for its share. How to eliminate?"
A: "No elimination needed - it's a real group expense. Only intercompany transactions eliminated."
Q: "Parent provides management services to subsidiary charging 100,000. How to treat?"
A: "Eliminate intercompany service revenue/expense: Dr. Other Income (Parent) 100,000, Cr. Administrative Expenses (Subsidiary) 100,000."
Q: "Subsidiary has preference shares held by parent. Are these equity or debt in consolidation?"
A: "If redeemable at subsidiary's option = liability. If redeemable at parent's option = equity. Check terms."
Q: "Goodwill on acquisition = 5,000,000. Need to test for impairment annually. How to calculate?"
A: "Compare carrying amount (5,000,000) with recoverable amount (higher of value in use or fair value less costs). If recoverable amount < 5,000,000, impair goodwill."
Q: "Subsidiary has foreign operations. Consolidation exchange difference = 200,000 loss. Where to book?"
A: "Book in Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) under 'Foreign Currency Translation Reserve'. Does not hit P&L."
Q: "Parent owns 70% of Subsidiary A, which owns 60% of Subsidiary B. How to calculate minority interest in B?"
A: "Minority in B = 40% of B's net assets. Group share in B = 70% × 60% = 42%. Direct parent ownership in B? If none, remaining 58% is with A's minority and B's minority."
Q: "Intercompany account shows parent receivable from subsidiary 100,000, but subsidiary shows payable to parent 95,000. Difference 5,000. How to resolve?"
A: "Likely due to goods in transit, timing differences, or errors. Reconcile: 1) Check cutoff 2) Identify missing entries 3) If unresolved, eliminate at lower amount (95,000) and 5,000 as reconciling item."
Q: "Subsidiary has tax loss carried forward of 2,000,000. Parent can't use it. How to treat deferred tax?"
A: "Recognize DTA only if probable that subsidiary will have future taxable profit. Otherwise, no DTA. Disclose unrecognized tax losses."
Q: "During year, parent increased stake in subsidiary from 60% to 80%. How to account?"
A: "Step acquisition. Previous 60%: equity method. Additional 20%: purchase method. Goodwill calculated on 20% purchase. Adjust previously held interest to fair value."
Q: "Subsidiary has non-controlling interest put option exercisable at fair value. How to treat?"
A: "Classify as financial liability at present value of redemption amount. Increases liability, decreases equity."
Q: "Group has defined benefit pension plan. Subsidiary contributes. How to consolidate?"
A: "Combine all plan assets/liabilities. Surplus/deficit recognized in balance sheet. Service cost in P&L, remeasurements in OCI."
Q: "Parent sells asset to subsidiary at profit. Asset has 5-year life. How to eliminate profit over time?"
A: "Year 1: Eliminate 100% of profit. Years 2-5: As asset depreciates, profit realization = profit/5 each year. Reverse elimination proportionally."
Q: "Subsidiary pays royalty to parent for technology. How to eliminate?"
A: "Dr. Other Income (Parent royalty income), Cr. Administrative/Other Expenses (Subsidiary). Net effect zero."
Q: "Intercompany dividend declared but not paid at year-end. How to treat?"
A: "Dividend receivable/payable remains in balance sheet. Eliminate: Dr. Dividend Payable (Sub), Cr. Dividend Receivable (Parent)."
Q: "Subsidiary has share-based payment to employees. Parent guarantees settlement. How to account?"
A: "If parent obligation, recognize liability in parent. Eliminate against subsidiary's equity-settled payment."
Q: "Based on the data, calculate Current Ratio for Mar'25."
A: "From ratio table: Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities = Not provided directly but formula given. Need current assets and liabilities from balance sheet."
Q: "Debt-Equity Ratio is provided as formula. From balance sheet: Total Debt = 2,978,504.92, Equity = 12,063,678.39. Calculate D/E."
A: "Debt-Equity Ratio = 2,978,504.92 / 12,063,678.39 = 0.247 or 24.7%. Acceptable < 2:1."
Q: "Inventory Turnover Ratio is 5.04. What does this indicate?"
A: "Inventory turns 5.04 times per year = sells inventory every 72 days (365/5.04). Industry benchmark needed, but generally >4 is good."
Q: "Trade Receivables Turnover = 5.79. Calculate average collection period."
A: "Collection period = 365 / 5.79 = 63 days. Means average 63 days to collect receivables."
Q: "Net Profit Ratio = 3% (1,015,511.65 / 32,501,794.17). Is this healthy?"
A: "3% net margin is low for manufacturing/trading. Should benchmark against industry. Could indicate high costs, low pricing, or inefficiencies."
Q: "Return on Capital Employed = 0.11 or 11%. How to interpret?"
A: "11% ROCE means for every 100 of capital, generates 11 profit. Should exceed cost of capital (say 8-10%). 11% is marginally acceptable."
Q: "Calculate Quick Ratio if Inventory = 4,827,046.44, Current Assets = 15,000,000 (est), Current Liabilities = 6,000,000 (est)."
A: "Quick Ratio = (Current Assets - Inventory) / Current Liabilities = (15,000,000 - 4,827,046.44) / 6,000,000 = 10,172,953.56 / 6,000,000 = 1.70. Good >1."
Q: "Gross Margin shown month-wise: Jan 156,445 on sales 305,693 = 51.2%. Feb 101,383 on 245,235 = 41.3%. Why decline?"
A: "Margin dropped 10%. Possible reasons: 1) Discounts increased 2) Product mix changed 3) COGS increased. Flag for investigation."
Q: "From cash flow perspective, company has operating cash flow positive but investing cash flow negative due to PPE additions. What stage is company?"
A: "Growth stage - investing in capacity expansion. Monitor if operating cash flow covers investing needs. If not, may need financing."
Q: "Calculate Interest Coverage Ratio if EBIT = 1,802,780.44, Interest Expense = 123.62 (from Note 25)."
A: "Interest Coverage = EBIT / Interest = 1,802,780.44 / 123.62 = 14,580 times. Extremely high - check if interest expense complete (maybe only part period)."
Q: "Asset Turnover Ratio = Sales / Total Assets. Sales = 32,501,794.17, Total Assets from balance sheet?"
A: "Need total assets. If assume 20,000,000, Asset Turnover = 32.5/20 = 1.63. Means 1.63 sales per asset rupee."
Q: "Calculate EBITDA from available data: Net Profit = 1,015,511.65, Tax = say 300,000, Interest = 123.62, Depreciation = from PPE note."
A: "Depreciation from Note: For Mar'25, Charge = 74,144 + 53,977 + 6,733 = ~134,854. EBITDA = 1,015,511.65 + 300,000 + 123.62 + 134,854 = ~1,450,489."
Q: "Days Payable Outstanding = 365 / Payables Turnover. Payables Turnover = 8.81. Calculate DPO."
A: "DPO = 365 / 8.81 = 41.4 days. Company pays suppliers on average 41 days."
Q: "Cash Conversion Cycle = Inventory Days + Receivable Days - Payable Days. Calculate."
A: "Inventory Days = 365/5.04 = 72.4. Receivable Days = 63.0. Payable Days = 41.4. CCC = 72.4 + 63.0 - 41.4 = 94 days. Capital tied for 94 days."
Q: "Return on Equity = 8% (0.08 from table). If industry average is 15%, what does lower ROE indicate?"
A: "Lower ROE could indicate: 1) Low profitability 2) High equity base 3) Suboptimal capital structure 4) Inefficient operations."
Q: "Calculate Working Capital = Current Assets - Current Liabilities. From ratio: Net Capital Turnover = Sales/Working Capital = 3.89. Working Capital = 32,501,794.17/3.89 = 8,355,000."
A: "Working Capital ≈ 8.36 million. Positive WC means sufficient short-term assets to cover liabilities."
Q: "Debt Service Coverage Ratio = 199.75. Is this safe?"
A: "DSCR > 1.5 is comfortable. 199.75 is extremely high - likely because denominator (debt service) is very small relative to cash flow."
Q: "Calculate Basic EPS if Net Profit = 1,015,511.65, Shares outstanding = 1,177,000 (from equity)."
A: "EPS = 1,015,511.65 / 1,177,000 = 0.863 per share."
Q: "From month-wise data, which month has highest sales and why?"
A: "Mar'25: 2,722,544 sales (highest). Possible year-end push, seasonal demand, or large orders."
Q: "If company wants to improve Current Ratio from 1.5 to 2.0, what options?"
A: "1) Increase current assets (collect receivables faster, liquidate inventory) 2) Reduce current liabilities (pay debts, convert to long-term) 3) Inject equity cash."
Q: "What disclosures are required for Property, Plant & Equipment under Ind AS 16?"
A: "1) Gross block, accumulated dep, net block by class 2) Depreciation method and rates 3) Additions, disposals 4) Impairment 5) Assets pledged as security."
Q: "Note 29 shows related parties. What minimum disclosures required under Ind AS 24?"
A: "1) Nature of relationship 2) Transactions during period 3) Balances at period end 4) Terms and conditions 5) Provisions for doubtful debts 6) Compensation to KMP."
Q: "Company has foreign currency transactions. What Ind AS 21 disclosures needed?"
A: "1) Forex differences in P&L 2) Exchange rates used 3) Net investment in foreign operations 4) Hedge accounting if any."
Q: "Note 28 shows deferred tax reconciliation. What's required under Ind AS 12?"
A: "1) Movement in deferred tax assets/liabilities 2) Temporary differences 3) Unrecognized DTAs (tax losses) 4) Reconciliation of tax expense."
Q: "Company has leases under Ind AS 116. What disclosures?"
A: "1) Right-of-use assets by class 2) Lease liabilities (current/non-current) 3) Depreciation and interest 4) Maturity analysis 5) Lease commitments."
Q: "Note 38 shows defined benefit plans. What Ind AS 19 disclosures?"
A: "1) Present value of defined benefit obligation 2) Fair value of plan assets 3) Expense in P&L and OCI 4) Actuarial assumptions 5) Sensitivity analysis."
Q: "What segment reporting is required under Ind AS 108?"
A: "Report segments if revenue/profit/assets > 10% of total. Disclose: 1) Segment revenue, profit, assets 2) Reconciliation to consolidated figures."
Q: "Note shows 'Expected credit loss' on receivables. Ind AS 109 disclosure requirements?"
A: "1) ECL methodology and assumptions 2) Movement in loss allowance 3) Credit risk exposure 4) Financial instruments by stage."
Q: "Company has inventory. What Ind AS 2 disclosures?"
A: "1) Accounting policies (cost formula) 2) Inventory classification 3) Carrying amount 4) Amount recognized as expense 5) Write-downs/reversals."
Q: "What events after reporting period need disclosure under Ind AS 10?"
A: "Material events between balance sheet date and authorization date: 1) Adjusting events (errors, settlements) 2) Non-adjusting but disclosable (mergers, disasters)."
Q: "How should government grants be disclosed under Ind AS 20?"
A: "1) Nature of grants 2) Unfulfilled conditions 3) Expected repayment if conditions not met 4) Accounting policy."
Q: "What fair value disclosures under Ind AS 113?"
A: "1) Fair value hierarchy (Level 1, 2, 3) 2) Valuation techniques 3) Transfers between levels 4) For Level 3: sensitivity analysis."
Q: "Disclosure requirements for financial instruments risk under Ind AS 107?"
A: "1) Credit risk 2) Market risk (currency, interest rate) 3) Liquidity risk 4) Capital management."
Q: "How to disclose earnings per share under Ind AS 33?"
A: "1) Basic and diluted EPS 2) Numerator and denominator calculation 3) Reconciliation with profit 4) Anti-dilutive instruments excluded."
Q: "What interim financial reporting requirements under Ind AS 34?"
A: "Condensed balance sheet, P&L, cash flow, equity changes, selected notes. Comparative periods."
Q: "Disclosure of changes in accounting policies under Ind AS 8?"
A: "1) Nature of change 2) Reason for change 3) Transitional provisions 4) Impact on current/prior periods."
Q: "How to disclose non-current assets held for sale under Ind AS 105?"
A: "1) Description of assets 2) Carrying amount 3) Expected timing of sale 4) Impairment losses/reversals."
Q: "What joint arrangement disclosures under Ind AS 111?"
A: "1) Nature, structure of arrangements 2) Accounting policy 3) Contingent liabilities 4) Capital commitments."
Q: "Disclosure of operating segments if not reported as segments?"
A: "If no segments reported, disclose: 1) Revenue from external customers 2) Carrying amount of assets 3) Additions to PPE - all by geographical area and products."
Q: "How to disclose contingent assets/liabilities under Ind AS 37?"
A: "Contingent liabilities: 1) Nature 2) Estimated financial effect 3) Uncertainties 4) Possible reimbursement. Contingent assets: disclose if probable inflow."
Q: "During upload, file has negative values for expense accounts (like -0.01 for Contributions to funds). How to flag?"
A: "Flag with warning: 'Negative expense detected. Could be reversal or error. Please review.' Confidence score 70%."
Q: "Balance sheet doesn't balance: Assets 15,000,000, Liabilities+Equity 14,950,000. Difference 50,000. How to identify cause?"
A: "Check: 1) Missing accounts 2) Incorrect signs (debit/credit) 3) Data entry errors 4) Foreign currency rounding 5) Intercompany mismatches."
Q: "Account 'Other Debtors' shows credit balance (negative). Is this valid?"
A: "Credit balance in debtor account = payable. Flag: 'Account 14010020 shows credit balance. Consider reclassification to payable accounts.' Confidence 85%."
Q: "Depreciation rate on computers appears 80% (74,751 gross, 60,123 dep). Is this reasonable?"
A: "Flag: 'High accumulated depreciation (80%). Computers typically 3-5 year life (20-33% p.a.). Verify useful life and method.' Confidence 90%."
Q: "Sales incentives-Provision shows negative (97,156) in June. What does this mean?"
A: "Negative provision = reversal of excess provision. Flag: 'Large provision reversal detected. Verify if actual incentives paid less than provisioned.'"
Q: "Trade Receivables Turnover Ratio 5.79 vs Industry average 8.0. Should we flag?"
A: "Flag as warning: 'Receivables collection slower than industry. Could indicate credit policy issues or collection problems.'"
Q: "Intercompany loan to Chemopharm (1,750,000) but no interest income shown. Should there be?"
A: "Flag: 'Intercompany loan exists but no interest income/expense. Verify if interest-free (may have transfer pricing implications).'"
Q: "Deferred tax asset decreased significantly from Mar'25 (56,110) to Jun'25 (28,196). Why?"
A: "Flag: 'Large DTA decrease in 3 months (50% reduction). Verify: 1) Utilization of tax losses 2) Change in probability of realization 3) Accounting error.'"
Q: "Month-wise sales: Jan 305,693, Feb 245,235, Mar 2,722,544. March spike normal?"
A: "Flag: 'March sales 11x February. Possible year-end acceleration or large one-time order. Verify cutoff and revenue recognition.'"
Q: "Multiple bank accounts with similar currencies: Alliance USD, CIMB USD. Why not consolidate?"
A: "Flag info: 'Multiple USD accounts detected. Consider consolidating for efficiency unless operational reasons.'"
Q: "Payables ageing shows mostly current. But some vendors may be overdue. How to identify?"
A: "Flag if: Payment terms exceeded based on invoice dates. Calculate days overdue = Today - Due Date."
Q: "Inventory write-off provision exists but no actual write-off in period. Normal?"
A: "Flag: 'Provision for inventory write-off exists but no actual write-off. Verify if inventory actually obsolete or provision excessive.'"
Q: "Employee count constant but salary expense varies monthly. Why?"
A: "Flag: 'Headcount constant but salaries vary. Possible: Bonuses, overtime, arrears, or data issues.'"
Q: "Gross margin fluctuates monthly (51% to 41%). Acceptable?"
A: "Flag: 'Gross margin volatility high. Investigate: Product mix changes, pricing discounts, input cost fluctuations.'"
Q: "Company has related party transactions but no disclosure of terms (interest rates, pricing)."
A: "Flag: 'Related party transactions lack pricing terms. Required for arm's length compliance and disclosure.'"
